plainTranslation: Drive and desire flow in sync. You move at the same pace, want similar things, and rarely step on each other. Failure mode: so frictionless it can lack tension. Enjoy the ease; keep some edge.
policy: Governed by synastry-policy. Descriptive, not deterministic; intensity is never treated as obligation, safety concerns override astrology.
note: Synced from authored synastry bundle synastry-authored__19_ (2).json.
summaryDeep:
You and this person tend to meet action with action in a way that feels natural. One of you starts moving and the other usually falls into step. Decisions do not require much negotiation. Getting things done together often feels easier than getting things done alone.

When this works, there is very little friction around effort. You encourage each other without pushing too hard. You trust each other's judgment under pressure. Even when you disagree, it is less likely to turn into a struggle over who gets to lead because you generally understand where the other person is coming from.

In everyday life, this can look like plans that actually happen, responsibilities that get shared without much discussion, and problems that get solved before they become bigger than they need to be. The two of you often spend more energy moving forward than arguing about how to move forward.

This ease tends to extend to the physical side as well. Mars is the body as much as the will, and when two drives move in the same spirit, attraction usually flows without much friction. You may find the physical rhythm between you feels natural and unforced, the same way the rest of your energy does. It is easy, which is lovely, and like everything easy here, it still does better when you actually keep showing up for it.

One thing to watch for is becoming comfortable with the potential instead of using it. Because working together feels so easy, you may assume there will always be time to act on your ideas. It becomes easy to talk about what you could do instead of actually doing it. Plans never quite become action. You know you make a good team, but you do not always challenge yourselves to put that strength to work.

The opportunity here is to be intentional. Give yourselves a goal that matters. Choose something you want to create, improve, or accomplish together, then take the first step. The teamwork is already in place. The more you channel it into real action, the more rewarding and productive this connection becomes.
